name: mail
documentation: The Mail plugin — a native, dependency-free MailPort adapter, a rich MailerContract, and a complete port of the Mailtrap API. Transports: SMTP (TLS/STARTTLS, AUTH PLAIN/LOGIN/CRAM-MD5/XOAUTH2, multi-host failover, keep-alive), Mailtrap Sending API (transactional/bulk/sandbox streams, stored templates, category, custom variables, batch send, per-message ids), Sendmail, PHP mail(), Array/Log (test/dev). Message API: from/sender/return-path, to/cc/bcc, reply-to, HTML + auto plain-text alternative, file/raw/inline-CID attachments, custom headers, priority, read receipts, charset, and the provider fields category/customVariables/template. MailtrapApiContract publishes the whole management API — accounts, API tokens, billing, permissions, users, sub-accounts, organizations, contacts/lists/fields/imports/events/exports, campaigns, email templates, sending domains, company info, email logs, stats, suppressions, tracking opt-outs, webhooks, sandbox projects/inboxes/messages/attachments, and inbound folders/inboxes/threads/messages incl. reply/replyAll/forward. Security: CR/LF header-injection guards on every address/header/param, TLS peer verification, DKIM RSA-SHA256 signing (relaxed/relaxed) on the MIME transports, hidden BCC, API tokens redacted from every debug and trace surface, and MailtrapWebhookSignature for verifying inbound delivery webhooks. send()/queue()/dispatchBatch() (queue via QueuePort + the mail.send job, which carries either built MIME or the serialised Message depending on the transport); views render through ViewRendererContract when present, else the view string is treated as raw HTML. MAIL_TRANSPORT=mailtrap and MailtrapApiContract both need an HttpClientPort in the request's dependency graph — this module declares no requires[], so install the HttpClient plugin and reach it via the consuming module's requires[], proj.json "essentials", or a withPorts() binding. Config in config/mail.php (MAIL_* / MAILTRAP_* env).
